title: Grill — Create all PRs: right title/body, right base, base-aware PR link
summary:
Before this gets planned: **13 decisions** the build would otherwise make silently, plus a short confirm-or-override list at the end.

Start with **Q1** (what the two real PRs actually got). It's the one place where your account and the code disagree. Then the **base** section, which decides whether we add migration `092`, and the **attribution** section, which decides how a proposal gets matched to a repository.

Source: the pipeline's overall goal (it isn't in the repo yet) and the investigation brief `docs/plans/create-all-prs-title-and-base-investigation.md`.

proven.text: **Why the titles were wrong.** Create all PRs matches a proposal to a repository only through a `Repository: <name>` line. Your pipeline's "Commit And Push" step reuses the *single-repo* prompt text, so the reply had no such lines. Both repositories fell back to `task.title` (the step's "`<pipeline>` · Commit And Push") with an **empty body**. A spike on the real reply printed `labeled blocks: 0`, `map size for 2 targets: 0`.

evidence.label: the fallback
evidence.code:
await api.createGitHubPull({
            path: projectPath,
            title: proposal?.title || task.title,
            head,
            base: defaults.base,

proven.text: **A latent wrong-repo bug.** When exactly one repository is targeted (a retry, or one repo left), the reply's *last* unlabeled proposal is attributed to it, even when it was written for another repo. On the real reply the app repo would get the infra PR's title and body.

**Why the base was wrong.** Every PR's base is `origin/HEAD` (or the literal `"main"` when that's unset). Nothing reads the branch the task was created from, and the task can't supply it anyway: `createTask` stores only the base **sha**, so the branch name you picked in the base picker is thrown away.

proven: **The real infra task was created from a non-default branch.** Its pinned sha is exactly the tip of a remote feature branch, while `origin/HEAD` is `main`.

**The create-time base isn't always right either.** Mid-pipeline the agent reset the app repo's task branch onto `origin/main`, so its pinned feature-branch base went stale and `main` was correct. Only the agent's reply knew that (it said so in prose).

**The prompt's link always targets the default branch.** `commitPushPrompt` asks for the link git prints on push (`…/pull/new/<branch>`), which opens a PR against the default branch. It's shared by the RunPanel chip, `agetor commit` and the TUI `c` key.

**Link-based attribution works on the real reply.** Matching each proposal's link against a repository's remote owner/name plus its live head attributed 3 of 3 proposals. Two matched the two repos. The third was a second branch in the app repo. A GitHub `compare/<base>...<head>` link also gives the base unambiguously, since git refs can't contain `..`.
**No test would catch either bug today.** The two e2e Create all PRs tests check only the PR count, `Closes #N` and the stamps. Nothing checks the title, the base, or attribution.
**The canned multi-repo prompt has never been sent in prod** (zero `run_events` hits), so the labeled format Create all PRs relies on has never appeared in real use.

sections.title: What actually happened
sections.intro: One place where the goal and the code disagree. The investigation couldn't read the real PRs (`gh` isn't logged in here).

questions.title: The goal says Create all PRs "is not creating the PR" when the target isn't the default branch. What actually happened to the two real PRs?
questions.why: If creation actually *failed* (a 422), there is a second root cause the investigation didn't find, and the plan needs another task for it.
questions.context: The code always sends `origin/HEAD` as the base, and **both** repository entries in the prod DB were stamped with a PR URL. That points to *opened against the wrong base*, not *not created*. Please check the infra PR on GitHub.

evidence.label: RunPanel stamps a repo only after createGitHubPull resolves

options.label: Both opened, but against `main` with the step title and an empty body
options.consequence: Matches the investigation. No extra root cause.

options.label: The infra PR failed with an error
options.description: Please paste the toast text in the note.
options.consequence: Adds an investigation task to the plan for a second root cause.

options.label: It opened against `main` and I closed it or retargeted it by hand
options.consequence: Same as the first option. Your manual fix is what we automate.

options.label: I'll check and tell you

recommendation.reason: Both entries carry a PR URL, and the stamp is written only after the create call succeeds.

sections.title: Which branch each PR targets
sections.intro: These decide the base the button sends, and whether we add a migration.

questions.title: Rank the sources Create all PRs should take a repository's base branch from, first match wins.
questions.why: This is the core of the base fix. The order decides which source wins when two disagree.
questions.context:
The real case needs **the agent's link** to beat **the create-time base** (the app repo was moved onto `main` mid-run) and **the create-time base** to beat **`origin/HEAD`** (the infra repo was based on a feature branch).

The link's base is only trusted when the link's owner/repo and head match that repository's remote and live head (see Q6).

options.label: The base in the agent's newest matching PR link
options.description: e.g. `compare/develop...my-branch`. Old `pull/new/<branch>` links carry no base and are skipped.

options.label: The base branch recorded when the task was created
The remote's default branch (`origin/HEAD`, then the provider's default)

recommendation.reason: That's the only order that gets both real repositories right.

questions.title: Record the base branch's name when a task is created?
questions.why: Yes means migration `092` (one-way, like every migration) plus a new server-managed column. No means a non-default base is only ever known from the agent's link.

options.label: Store it (migration 092 plus `repositories[].baseBranch`)
options.consequence: Fixes the infra case even when the agent prints an old-style link. One more migration and server-managed column.

options.label: Don't store it; infer it from git at PR time
options.description: Pick the remote branch whose tip is the nearest ancestor of the head.
options.consequence: No migration, and it works for existing tasks. A guess, though: it picks wrongly when several branches share history, and it costs extra git calls on each press.

options.label: Don't store it; rely on the agent's link only
options.consequence: Smallest change. An old-style link, or an agent that ignores the ask, opens against the default branch, which is today's bug.

recommendation.reason: It's the only deterministic source for a non-default base when the agent doesn't cooperate, and it also lets the prompt name the base (Q12).

questions.title: When the task's base is `HEAD` (no branch picked), what should be recorded as its base branch?
questions.why: `HEAD` is the default for most tasks, so this decides whether the stored base helps in the common case.
questions.context: With `HEAD`, the task branches from whatever the source repo has checked out at create time, for example a feature branch you were standing on.

options.label: The checked-out branch, but only if it exists on the remote
options.consequence: A local-only or detached checkout records nothing and falls back to `origin/HEAD`.

options.label: The checked-out branch, always
options.consequence: A local-only branch becomes a base the remote doesn't have, so the PR fails (Q5).

options.label: Nothing: only an explicitly picked branch is recorded
options.consequence: `HEAD` tasks keep falling back to `origin/HEAD`.

recommendation.reason: It covers branching while standing on a feature branch without inventing a base the remote doesn't have.

questions.title: The chosen base doesn't exist on the remote (deleted, never pushed, typo in the agent's link). What happens to that repository?
questions.why: Today GitHub answers 422 and the toast shows a raw API message.

options.label: Fail that repository with a clear message
options.description: e.g. "infra: base branch `develop` isn't on origin". Other repos continue, and a retry is possible (per-repo best effort, as today).
options.consequence: No surprise PRs. You fix the base and press again (or use the confirm list, Q9).

options.label: Fall through to the next source in the Q2 order
options.consequence: Always opens a PR, but possibly against the default branch. That's the bug we're fixing, just less often.

recommendation.reason: A PR against the wrong base shows someone else's commits, which is worse than a clear failure you can retry.

sections.title: Which proposal belongs to which repository

questions.title: How should Create all PRs match a proposal to a repository?
questions.why: This fixes the wrong titles. It also decides what happens to today's "one unlabeled proposal → the one target" fallback, which causes the wrong-repo bug.
questions.context:
A proposal's link is already parsed (`PrProposal.link`) but nothing reads it.

Link match means:
- the link's host and owner/repo equal that repository's remote (from `/github/provider-info`);
- **and** its head branch equals the repository's live PR head.

It's also the trust bound: an agent-written URL can never attribute a title to another repository or head.

options.label: Link match OR a `Repository:` label; drop the blind single-target fallback
options.description: A labeled block whose link names another repo is ignored for that repo.
options.consequence: Fixes the real reply (3/3) and the latent bug. Breaks the `pr-proposal.test.ts:628` case, which changes on purpose.

options.label: Link match OR label; keep the single-target fallback only when the proposal has no link at all
options.consequence: Same fixes, but a linkless proposal can still be misattributed when there's one target.

options.label: Labels only; fix the pipeline prompt instead
options.consequence: Your existing pipeline keeps producing empty-body PRs until you edit it.

recommendation.reason: Every prompt asks for a link, so a linkless proposal is rare, and guessing its repo is exactly what caused the wrong-repo bug.

questions.title: Which run's proposal counts for each repository?
questions.why: Today the newest run that contains *any* proposal wins outright, so a later turn that proposes only one repo hides the other repo's proposal from an earlier turn.

options.label: Per repository: its newest matching proposal from any run
options.description: Still bounded by the live head and remote match.
options.consequence: Committing repo A in one turn and repo B in a later one still works. A stale proposal from an old run on the same branch can win if nothing newer exists.

options.label: Keep it: only the newest run that proposed anything
options.consequence: Simpler. A split commit-and-push across turns loses the earlier repo's title.

recommendation.reason: Agents (and pipelines) often push repos in separate turns, and the head match keeps stale proposals for other branches out.

questions.title: No proposal matches a repository. What should its PR get?
questions.why: Today it gets `task.title`, which for a pipeline step is "`<pipeline>` · Commit And Push", and an empty body.

options.label: The root task's title (the pipeline parent's, for a step) and an empty body, marked "no proposal" in the confirm list
options.consequence: Never blocks, never uses a step name. Relies on Q9 to show you before creating.

options.label: Skip that repository: "no PR proposal found, run Commit & push first"
options.consequence: No placeholder PRs. Someone who pushed by hand can't use the button for that repo.

options.label: Keep today's behavior (`task.title`, empty body)

recommendation.reason: Keeps the button useful after a manual push while removing the step-name title that started this.

sections.title: What you see before and while creating

questions.title: Keep Create all PRs one-click, or show a short confirm list first?
questions.why: PRs are outward-facing (reviewers get notified), and a wrong base shows someone else's commits, so this is the safety net for every guess above.

options.label: Confirm list, editable
options.description: One row per repository: `head → base` (base editable from the remote's branches), title (editable) and a "no proposal" or "base from: link / task / default" hint. Then Create.
options.consequence: New dialog, its tests and an e2e step. Catches every bad guess before it becomes a public PR.
options.preview:
Create pull requests
─────────────────────────────────────────────
 app    fix/x → [main     ▾]   base from: link
        Title: [fix: handle empty config      ]
 infra  fix/x → [develop  ▾]   base from: task
        Title: [fix: retry on 502             ]
─────────────────────────────────────────────
                         [Cancel] [Create 2 PRs]

options.label: Confirm list, read-only
options.description: Same rows, but no editing. To change something, cancel and use the single Create PR composer.
options.consequence: Less UI. Fixing a bad base takes more clicks.

options.label: One-click, as today
options.description: The toast reports each repo's base afterwards.
options.consequence: Smallest change. A bad guess becomes a public PR before you see it.

recommendation.reason: Every base source here can be wrong (stale create-time base, agent typo), and fixing it before the PR is public costs one click, not a closed PR.

questions.title: Should the single-repo "Create PR" chip also prefill the composer's base from the proposal?
questions.why: Without it, the new base-aware link improves Create all PRs but the single-repo path still defaults to `origin/HEAD`.
questions.context: That means adding `base?` to `GitHubPullPrefill` and making sure the defaults effect doesn't overwrite it. The same Q2 order applies: link, then the stored base, then the default.

options.label: Yes, same base rules as Create all PRs
options.consequence: Both PR paths agree.

options.label: No, out of scope

recommendation.reason: Single-repo tasks hit the same non-default-base bug, and leaving that path out would look unfinished.

sections.title: The Commit & push prompt (single and multi; RunPanel chip, `agetor commit`, TUI `c`)

questions.title: Which link should the prompt ask the agent to print?
questions.why: The goal asks for a link that already targets the destination branch. The format decides what the parser reads the base from.
questions.context:
- **GitHub** (documented): `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/compare/<base>...<head>?quick_pull=1`. `expand=1` is common but undocumented.
- **GitLab** (community-sourced): `…/-/merge_requests/new?merge_request[source_branch]=<head>&merge_request[target_branch]=<base>`.
- **Bitbucket Cloud** (community-sourced): `…/pull-requests/new?source=<head>&dest=<base>`.

If the GitLab or Bitbucket parameters don't work, the link still opens the new-PR page, just without the target preselected.

evidence.label: GitHub: query parameters for a new PR

options.label: Per-forge destination links: GitHub `compare/…?quick_pull=1`, GitLab `target_branch`, Bitbucket `dest`
options.consequence: The parser reads the base from all three forms.

options.label: GitHub compare link only; keep "whatever git prints" for others
options.consequence: GitLab and Bitbucket PRs keep targeting the default branch.

options.label: Per-forge, but GitHub with `expand=1`
options.consequence: Opens the full form instead of the quick one. Undocumented.

recommendation.reason: Create all PRs already works on all three forges, and `quick_pull=1` is the documented GitHub form.

questions.title: Should the prompt name the base agetor already knows?
questions.why: Naming it makes the agent's link match the task by default. It's also only possible if Q3 stores the base (otherwise all we know is `origin/HEAD`).
questions.context: For example: "target `develop` unless you moved this branch onto another base; then target that one." In a multi-repo prompt, the base goes on each repository line. The CLI and TUI build the same prompt from the same `Task`, so they get it for free.

options.label: Name the known base, with "unless you moved the branch onto another base"
options.consequence: Handles the real app-repo case (reset onto `main`). Adds a clause per repository.

options.label: Name it and require it
options.consequence: The app-repo case would have targeted the stale feature branch.

options.label: Don't name it; let the agent work out the destination
options.consequence: Shorter prompt. The agent guesses, and often guesses the default branch.

recommendation.reason: The real run needed both: the known base for infra, and the agent's own judgment for the app repo.

questions.title: Should the agent also print an explicit `Base: <branch>` line?

options.label: No, the link carries the base
options.consequence: One source per proposal, so the line and the link can never disagree.

options.label: Yes, plus the link
options.consequence: Easier to parse and works if a forge link format is wrong. Adds a rule for when the line and the link disagree.

recommendation.reason: A compare link already states the base unambiguously, and a second copy just adds a conflict case.

questions.title: The real reply proposed two PRs for the app repo (a second branch). Support more than one PR per repository?
questions.why: Today the model is one PR per repository, headed at its live checkout.

options.label: Out of scope: one PR per repository, its live head
options.description: A proposal for another branch is ignored by Create all PRs, and the confirm list doesn't show it.
options.consequence: The second branch's PR stays manual (the link in the reply still works).

options.label: In scope: one PR per matching proposal
options.consequence: New stamping model (`prUrl` per repository becomes a list), which changes the data shape. A different-sized change.

recommendation.reason: It's a different feature with its own data change. This ticket is about the right title and base for the one PR.

questions.title: Your pipeline's "Commit And Push" step text is an old copy of the single-repo prompt. What do we do about it?
questions.why: That text lives in your pipeline definition in the agetor DB, not in this repo.

options.label: Nothing in code; link attribution covers it. I'll update my own step text myself.
options.consequence: The plan notes the new prompt text so you can paste it.

options.label: Same, and the docs say pipeline authors should reuse the canned prompt's wording
options.consequence: One paragraph in `docs/architecture/pipelines.md`.

recommendation.reason: The code fix covers your pipeline either way, and a note keeps the next pipeline author from copying the old text.

sections.title: Confirm or override
sections.intro: Defaults I'd bet on. One click each.

questions.title: Existing tasks

recommendation.value: No backfill. Existing tasks have no stored base and fall through to the next source in the Q2 order.
recommendation.reason: One pinned sha matched three refs, so any backfill would be a guess.

questions.title: Base name normalization

recommendation.value: A picked `origin/develop` is stored as `develop` (the remote prefix is stripped when it names a configured remote). Links are URL-decoded (`release%2F1.2` → `release/1.2`).
recommendation.reason: PR APIs take the bare branch name.

questions.title: Old transcripts

recommendation.value: Old `pull/new/<branch>` links still attribute a proposal (by owner/repo and head), with no base taken from them.
recommendation.reason: Existing transcripts and agents that ignore the new ask keep working.

questions.title: Acceptance tests

recommendation.value: Unit tests for link parsing, attribution and base precedence. Updated prompt tests. A new `FAKE_CLAUDE_*_PROMPT_MARKER` that emits proposal text on the assistant stream, plus an e2e that drives Create all PRs and asserts each PR's **title, body and base** through the GitHub stub's recorded POST bodies, including a repository with a non-default base.
recommendation.reason: No test checks the title or base today, so the fix needs one that can fail.

questions.title: Docs updated in the same change

recommendation.value: `docs/architecture/multi-repo-tasks.md` (pull-create section), `docs/architecture/run-panel.md` (Create all PRs), `docs/architecture/persistence.md` (new server-managed column, if Q3 = store), the CLAUDE.md server-managed list, the `commitPushPrompt` and `pr-proposal.ts` header comments, and the Commit & push tooltip. `docs/plans/multi-repo-tasks.md` A10 marked superseded.
recommendation.reason: CLAUDE.md requires a doc update whenever a subsystem's behavior changes.

questions.title: PRs opened from a pipeline step's panel

recommendation.value: Unchanged: a PR opened from a step is stamped on the step only (already documented). Out of scope.
recommendation.reason: It's a separate, documented limitation, and this ticket doesn't touch stamping.
